## Observed Facts

- **Data Scope:** BGL dataset, full time range (2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04), no filters [E1]. The corpus holds 4,747,963 Log Entries [E1].
- **KERNEL is the largest Component by volume:** 4,324,651 Log Entries [E2], about 91% of the corpus.
- **KERNEL also leads FATAL entries:** 626,450 of 855,195 FATAL Log Entries [E4]. This is the largest single count of severe-level entries in the dataset.
- **APP is second on FATAL:** 228,536 FATAL Log Entries [E4].
- **MMCS leads ERROR entries:** 88,529 of 112,355 ERROR Log Entries [E5]. It has only 3 FATAL entries [E4].
- **DISCOVERY leads SEVERE entries:** 18,324 of 19,213 SEVERE Log Entries [E6]. It also has 23,825 ERROR entries [E5].
- **MONITOR leads FAILURE entries:** 1,665 of 1,714 FAILURE Log Entries [E7].
- **Data Scope for all counts above:** BGL, full time range, no Component or Node filter. The "level" and "component" filters were applied one at a time.

## Hypotheses

- **KERNEL is the biggest risk by measured frequency.** It has the most FATAL Log Entries [E4] and the most Log Entries overall [E2]. Both point the same way, so it is the first priority.
- **APP is the second priority.** It has 228,536 FATAL Log Entries [E4], over a quarter of the FATAL total [E3, E4].
- **MMCS and DISCOVERY are secondary.** They carry large ERROR and SEVERE counts [E5, E6] but much lower FATAL counts.
- **Frequency is not the same as severity.** The BGL level labels come from the log lines themselves. The logs show how often each label appears, not what each event cost.

## Unknowns

- Whether the FATAL labels in KERNEL and APP are real failures or routine messages. I measured the labels, not the outcomes.
- Whether these counts are growing, steady, or one-off spikes. I did not run a trend query.
- Any business, service, or customer impact, including downtime or financial loss. The logs cannot establish these.
- Whether the KERNEL and APP FATAL entries cluster on a few Nodes. I did not check Nodes.

## Next Step

Run a trend on KERNEL FATAL entries by week, and a count by node for the same filter. That will show whether the 626,450 entries are recurring across the period or concentrated in a few Nodes, which is the main thing that would change this priority.
